executive_summary: Feasibility-study module of the provincial Groningen scheme against grid congestion on business parks (Subsidieregeling Oplossen netcongestiebelemmeringen op bedrijventerreinen, Nationaal Programma Groningen), run by SNN. It funds a study by an independent expert, including quarter-hourly metering, that maps a company's energy use and generation and identifies solutions to the grid-congestion barriers it faces. Individual companies or collaborations of companies active in the province of Groningen may apply. The subsidy is 75% of eligible costs, up to EUR 10,000 for an individual company or EUR 15,000 for a collaboration, under de minimis rules, from a sub-budget of EUR 500,000 allocated first come, first served. Applications are open from 25 March 2025 to 1 July 2028; the study must be completed within 12 months.
status_rationale: The module funds an independent feasibility study, with quarter-hourly metering, of a company's energy situation and solutions to grid-congestion barriers on business parks in Groningen (Verordening Subsidieregeling Oplossen netcongestie bedrijventerreinen (NPG), art. 2, 5 lid 1 and 13 lid 1). It touches TenneT's field directly, since it targets congestion and flexible use of grid connections, sharing aims with the Lion Storage time-dependent transmission rights contract, the Energy boards and Grids & Benefits, but it acts behind the meter at grid users rather than in the grid. Only companies or collaborations of companies that experience congestion problems on a business park may apply (art. 2, 3 and 7), and the scheme sets out no role for a grid operator, so TenneT cannot take part. It fits C3.3 because the studies can lead to flexible loads, storage and better use of connections.
